scenes.text: Does having the biggest military guarantee that a country always wins?
scenes.narration: Imagine spending billions on weapons, only to watch your global influence shrink! Why do superpowers fail when they rely only on force? Let's decode power in international politics.

scenes.text: A class monitor who only threatens punishments loses friends, while respect wins cooperation.
scenes.narration: Think of this school analogy. If a class monitor only threatens punishments, classmates rebel. But when the monitor inspires others, everyone cooperates willingly without any fighting!

scenes.heading: Power Classification of Nations
scenes.narration: In world politics, nations rank by their strength. Superpowers project military force globally, while great powers protect themselves alone. Middle powers need coalitions, and small powers rely on others.

scenes.heading: Hard Power vs Soft Power
scenes.narration: Hard power uses state military and economic force to compel others immediately. In contrast, soft power is idealistic and diffused through society, winning long-term goodwill voluntarily.

scenes.name: Joseph Nye
scenes.idea: Smart power combines military strength with partnerships and institutions.
scenes.narration: Scholar Joseph Nye warned that relying solely on hard power damaged American hegemony. He proposed smart power: pairing military capability with diplomatic alliances, institutions, and partnerships.

scenes.heading: Speed Versus Heft
scenes.narration: Here's a new debate: John Chipman argues fast power and agility matter more today than sheer size. Yet critics counter that patient, well-considered choices beat hasty decisions.

scenes.heading: Trap of Unipolar Overstretch
scenes.narration: Can one superpower keep global peace? Realists Kenneth Waltz and Mearsheimer say no: policing the world causes imperial overstretch, encourages rival free riders, and sparks dangerous megalomania.

items: Elements become determinants only through skill.
Smart power balances military strength with partnerships.
Unipolar overstretch creates instability and conflict.
scenes.narration: Here's the trick to remember: resources become power only through skillful use, smart power beats pure force, and overstretched superpowers always invite instability.
